items.title: Syed Azman raises HHRG stake after taking chairman's seat
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Newly-appointed executive chairman Tan Sri Syed Azman Syed Ibrahim has raised his stake in biomass company HHRG Bhd by more than 4.7 million shares. The purchase price was 3.7 per cent above HHRG's closing price of 17.5 sen on Wednesday. Following the acquisition, Syed Azman's stake in HHRG stood at 3.21 per cent, keeping him below the five per cent threshold for substantial shareholders.

items.title: PM Anwar to meet Modi, Putin and other leaders during Brics Summit in New Delhi
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is set to engage in high-level bilateral meetings with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Russian President Vladimir Putin during his visit to the Indian capital for the 18th Brics Summit this weekend. “Besides Modi and Putin, the Prime Minister will also meet Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed on the sidelines of the Summit. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, will be accompanied by the Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and the Minister of Human Resources Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan.

items.title: Ringgit firmer against US dollar ahead of US CPI data
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed marginally higher against the US dollar on Thursday despite elevated crude oil prices and expectations of a possible US interest rate hike, as investors looked ahead to the release of US consumer price index (CPI) data on Friday. Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said Brent crude was hovering around US$101 per barrel, a development that could bolster the case for a rate hike at next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting. "Despite that, the ringgit performed favourably against the US dollar.

items.title: Missing person case reclassified as murder after man found dead in septic tank
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL: Police have reclassified a missing person case as murder after a man was found dead in a septic tank at a house in Taman Seri Bistari here yesterday. Seberang Prai Selatan deputy district police chief Deputy Superintendent Mohd Norazmi Abd Ghapar said a missing-person report was lodged on Sept 7, prompting an immediate investigation. "Based on the post-mortem findings and developments in the investigation, police have reclassified the case from Section 365 of the Penal Code for abduction to Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder," Norazmi said tonight.

items.title: Three suspects arrested in Alam Megah murder case, police thank public for vital leads
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have arrested three of seven suspects wanted to assist investigations into the Alam Megah murder in Section 28, here last month. Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the suspects, all locals in their 20s and 40s, were arrested between Sept 4 and 7 following leads from members of the public after their photographs were made public last Friday. Meanwhile, commenting on public calls for the proposed construction of a new police station in Puncak Alam following three successful operations to dismantle drug laboratories in the area, Shazeli said there are several key factors that need to be taken into consideration.

items.title: Akmal tells PH to forget BN cooperation for Melaka polls
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh has challenged Pakatan Harapan to contest all 28 seats in the next Melaka state election, telling the coalition to forget about working with Barisan Nasional. Forget about working with BN. Contest all 28 seats.

items.title: IHH Healthcare unit loses RM5.7bil claim against Japan's pharmaceutical giant
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: IHH Healthcare Bhd's Singapore-based unit Northern TK Venture Pte Ltd has lost a ¥200 billion (about RM5.7 billion) damages claim against Japanese pharmaceutical giant Daiichi Sankyo Co Ltd, after a Tokyo court dismisses all its claims. The Tokyo District Court on Thursday dismissed Northern TK's legal claims and ordered the IHH unit to bear the litigation costs, IHH said in a Bursa Malaysia filing. The claim, initially filed for ¥20 billion, was expanded to about ¥200 billion in May 2025 following an assessment of the losses Northern TK alleged it suffered due to its stalled Fortis Healthcare acquisition.

items.title: Malaysia property market remains resilient with RM105.12bil transactions in 1H 2026 – Amir Hamzah
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's property market remained resilient, recording 187,320 transactions worth RM105.12 billion in the first half of 2026 (1H 2026), Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said. Amir Hamzah said 27,832 new residential units were launched in 1H 2026, with a sales performance of 16.6 per cent. "The industrial property segment also grew 3.8 per cent, recording 3,932 transactions worth RM14.78 billion.

items.title: Op Fella widens: MACC wants prison access to question ex‑Felda chairman on asset deals
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) will seek the cooperation of the Malaysian Prison Department to record the statement of a former Felda chairman currently serving a prison sentence to assist its investigation into the assets and investments of Felda Investment Corporation (FIC). MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the statement needed to be recorded due to a link between the purchase of certain assets and FIC investments currently under investigation. Abd Halim said seven investigation papers had been opened to date under ‘Op Fella’, while statements from 29 witnesses had been recorded in investigations into alleged corruption involving asset purchases and investments by Felda and FIC.

items.title: LSH Capital gets nod to build, operate RM1.75bil Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan expressway
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lim Seong Hai Capital Bhd (LSH Capital) has received in-principle approval from the Cabinet to undertake the proposed RM1.75 billion Bandar Malaysia-Seri Kembangan Expressway (BSE). It will be undertaken under a build-operate-transfer privatisation arrangement, LSH Capital said in a statement. This includes the Kuala Lumpur-Seremban Expressway, SPE, East-West Link Expressway, New Pantai Expressway, Sungai Besi Expressway, MEX and PLUS.

items.title: Malaysia, India set to deepen trade, investment ties through BRICS
items.summary: Malaysia's total trade with India, however, fell 5.0 per cent to RM79.33 billion (US$18.55 billion) in 2025 from RM83.5 billion (US$18.25 billion) in 2024, mainly due to a sharp decline in imports. Malaysia's exports to India edged up 0.4 per cent to RM52.35 billion (US$12.25 billion) from RM52.13 billion (US$11.4 billion) in 2024, supported largely by higher shipments of non-metallic mineral products. Imports from India, meanwhile, fell 14 per cent to RM26.98 billion (US$6.29 billion) from RM31.37 billion (US$6.85 billion), mainly due to a RM4.23 billion, or 43.8 per cent, decline in petroleum product imports.

items.title: Toddler dies after being found unconscious at babysitter's home in Air Itam
items.summary: Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police received a report from the Penang Hospital Emergency and Trauma Department at 5.16pm on Sept 8 concerning the child's death. He said the 13-month-old Sabah-born indigenous child was found unconscious with bluish lips by the 44-year-old babysitter around 2pm. "Police have detained the babysitter and the child's mother to assist investigations," he said.

items.title: Malaysian woman dies in Perth after alleged domestic assault
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 28-year-old Malaysian woman residing in Perth, Australia, has died after allegedly being assaulted late last month. Tan Kah Ming was found unresponsive at a residence on Taree Street, St James, at 8.30pm on Aug 26, according to a 7News Australia report on Aug 28. Qambari was charged with murder on Aug 28 and appeared briefly before the Perth magistrate's court.

items.title: Judges Alice Loke and Elaine Yap take oaths, marking new appointments in Malaysian judiciary
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — High Court Judge Alice Loke Yee Ching today took her oath of office and allegiance as a Court of Appeal judge. Judicial Commissioner Elaine Yap Chin Gaik, meanwhile, took her oath of office and allegiance as a High Court judge. She was appointed a High Court Judicial Commissioner on July 10, 2020.

items.title: 'Give us space to lead today,' says Puteri Umno chief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Puteri Umno wants greater leadership opportunities now rather than being treated merely as the party's future, said its chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi. "If Puteri is the future, give us space to lead today. Listen to our voices, give us space, give us trust and give us responsibility.

items.title: Domestic violence must be taken seriously, says deputy minister
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Domestic violence must never be normalised, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying said, urging victims to seek help and protection and calling on society to remain vigilant against abuse. Lim expressed sadness over the death of Malaysian Tan Kah Ming, who was reportedly found unresponsive in Perth, Australia, in an incident believed to be linked to domestic violence. She said domestic violence could have profound effects on victims, their children, families and the wider community.

items.title: Anwar's India visit to boost trade, investment ties with key partner
items.summary: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's five-day working visit to India from Sept 11 to 15 is set to strengthen Malaysia's economic engagement with one of its key trading partners, with trade, investment and access to new markets high on the agenda. She said the visit will feature high-level bilateral talks, business engagements and Malaysia's participation in the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit. Anwar will meet Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sept 12 to explore trade and investment opportunities, alongside separate meetings with business leaders.

items.title: Malaysia ranks second in Asean digital nations index
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia ranked second among Asean countries in the GSMA's 2026 Digital Nations Index, behind Singapore. GSMA director-general Vivek Badrinath said Asean's target of building a US$2 trillion digital economy by 2030 would require greater coordination between national digital strategies. The final day of M360 Asean 2026 focused on connecting national digital strategies and developing a more integrated regional digital market as digital services become more widely adopted across Asean.

items.title: Super El Niño to torch Malaysia next March, MetMalaysia warns heat soaring past 40°C
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) expects temperatures in several parts of the country to exceed 40 degrees Celsius next year, driven by a Super El Niño phenomenon forecast to reach its strongest intensity on record. “The highest daily temperature ever recorded in the country was 40.1 degrees Celsius in Chuping, Perlis, during the Super El Niño phenomenon of 1997/1998. “Given that this phenomenon is forecast to be stronger than previous episodes, compounded by global warming, temperatures can surpass that record and reach 40.5 or even 41 degrees Celsius,” he said during an appearance on Bernama Radio’s Fokus 30 programme titled Super El Niño: Kesan Kepada Negara (Super El Niño: Impact on the Nation), today.

items.title: Bermaz Auto's Q1 earnings surge to RM40.5mil, revenue rises to RM553mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bermaz Auto Bhd's net profit jumped multifold to RM40.5 million in the first quarter of financial year 2026 (Q1 FY26) from RM8.28 million a year earlier, due to higher sales volume from its Mazda domestic operations. Bermaz Auto's revenue rose 12.6 per cent to RM553 million in the quarter ended July 31, 2026, from RM491 million last year. In a statement, the company said the better performance was driven mainly by higher sales volume from its Mazda domestic operations, particularly the Mazda3, which continued to receive a favourable response from consumers.

items.title: Respect Malay Rulers despite political differences, says Puteri Umno
items.summary: A Puteri Umno delegate Nur Atiqah Othman said differences of opinion and political competition were part of democracy, but the limits of respect for the institution that served as the country's constitutional pillar must not be crossed. "Political differences should never become a reason to question the institution that serves as the nation's umbrella. Umno will continue to defend the sovereignty of the Malay Rulers and the principles of constitutional monarchy," she said while debating the Puteri Umno chief's policy speech at the 2026 Umno General Assembly here today.

items.title: MACC to charge ex‑minister Monday over Tabung Haji RCI, probe assets in Saudi Arabia
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 10 — A former minister will be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court next Monday as part of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission’s (MACC) probe arising from the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Speaking at a special press conference at the MACC headquarters today, Abd Halim said the former minister was also linked to assets in Saudi Arabia. He said five people had been charged so far in the TH RCI probe: a former deputy general manager of construction and a former security and health manager at TH Properties Sdn Bhd, a former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman, Alam Maritim Sdn Bhd’s chief executive officer, and a former TH chief operating officer.

items.title: FDS heli crash: Remains to be released after DNA identification
items.summary: MIRI: The remains of all five victims of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash will be handed over to their families once DNA identification results are obtained. Sarawak Police Commissioner Datuk Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said post-mortems on the five victims were still being conducted at Miri Hospital following Tuesday's crash in Long Lellang. The remains will be handed over to the victims' families once the DNA test results are obtained," he said when contacted.

items.title: Anwar briefs Sultan of Selangor on state development
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today had an audience with the Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, to brief the ruler on state development matters. "During the meeting, I briefed His Royal Highness on several matters, including current issues involving the development of Selangor," Anwar said in a social media post today. Anwar also wished His Royal Highness and the royal family continued blessings, good health, well-being and sovereignty.

items.title: Lawyer claims Negri MB willingly signed proclamation to remove Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: SEREMBAN: A lawyer representing the dismissed Undang of Negri Sembilan; the Tunku Besar Tampin; and the Datuk Shahbandar, has claimed that Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim knowingly and willingly signed a proclamation to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir. Mohd Khairul Azam Abdul Aziz said Ismail's claim that he signed the proclamation against his will was an afterthought. Yesterday, Ismail, in a statement, said that the Instrument of Proclamation to remove the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, which he signed on Aug 3 at Istana Laguna Biru in Port Dickson, was signed " against his will and under duress ."

items.title: Puteri Umno urges respect for Pardons Board constitutional process
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Puteri Umno delegate has urged political parties "on the other side" not to pre-empt the constitutional process of the Pardons Board. Melaka Puteri Umno deputy chief Nur Farhana Ab Ghani also urged the parties not to create political pressure or shape public perceptions before the process takes place. Puteri Umno is not asking anyone to determine the Pardons Board's decision.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM SEPTEMBER 10, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's 30-stock index closed lower on Thursday amid cautious sentiment among investors following higher crude oil prices. The key index dropped more than eight points at the closing bell to 1,705. In the crypto exchange, Bitcoin dropped to RM319,380.

items.title: Police record 12 witness statements after RM2.91m armed gang robbery at Jalan Ampang condo
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Police have recorded the statements of 12 witnesses to assist investigations into an armed gang robbery at a luxury condominium in Jalan Ampang here, involving losses of RM2.91 million. In a statement today, Wangsa Maju police chief ACP Annas Sulaiman said they are still working to identify all the suspects involved. Those with information on the incident are urged to contact the Wangsa Maju district police control centre at 03-9289 9222, Kuala Lumpur police hotline at 03-2115 9999, or any nearby police station.

items.title: 'Don't invent what PH didn't say,' Kamil tells Asyraf"
items.summary: IPOH: Pakatan Harapan (PH) has never questioned the constitutional powers of the Yang di-Pertuan Agong to grant pardons, said PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim. Muhammad Kamil said PH respected the Federal Constitution and the country's institutions while maintaining its position against corruption and abuse of power. "PH's position is straightforward.

items.title: 'Just regular afternoon tea,' says Umno president's aide on Zahid-Negri MB meeting
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The meeting between Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim ended after two hours. Among those who attended the meeting, which started at about 4pm at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur, were Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan and all three Umno vice-presidents, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin and Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail. About 40 minutes later, Khaled was seen leaving the room.

items.title: MACC thanks RTD for cooperation in exposing vehicle ownership document syndicate
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has thanked the Road Transport Department (RTD) for its cooperation and intelligence-sharing, which helped expose a syndicate allegedly falsifying documents to facilitate vehicle ownership transfers in Perak. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said cooperation between the two enforcement agencies was instrumental in uncovering the syndicate's activities. The syndicate is suspected of falsifying vehicle ownership documents and bribing enforcement agency officers in Perak to facilitate changes to vehicle ownership status.

items.title: Guan Eng trial: Penang mayor to testify on Sept 28
items.summary: Witness: Correct. Witness: Correct. Witness: Correct.

items.title: AME Elite buys Pontian land for RM200mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: AME Elite Consortium Bhd is acquiring 71.43 hectares of freehold land in Pontian, Johor for RM199.8 million cash. The industrial space solutions provider said the acquisition will strengthen its Johor development footprint. AME Elite executive director and group chief executive officer Dylan Tan Teck Eng said the acquisition would enable the group to capitalise on growing foreign and domestic direct investment flows into Johor.

items.title: Petronas-Petros deal could face ‘Tabung Haji’ reckoning in future, warns expert
items.summary: Walter Sandosam said the political circumstances surrounding any agreement could later come under scrutiny, even if it is defended today as a practical solution. “Petronas-Petros could become a future accountability issue if a settlement is seen as political compromise rather than national-interest decision,” he said. “This creates space for political horse-trading,” he said.

items.title: Sarawak dominates unhealthy API readings, Serian highest at 183
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Serian recorded the country's highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 183 as of 5.30pm today, with 11 areas nationwide recording unhealthy air quality. Another 52 areas recorded moderate air quality, with Johor registering some of the highest readings — Kota Tinggi (95), Pengerang (93), Kluang (92), Batu Pahat (90) and Tangkak (88). Several areas in Sarawak also recorded moderate readings, including Bintulu (86), Miri (83), ILP Miri (79), Kapit (74) and Limbang (71).

items.title: New Hoong Fatt to park RM20mil in venture fund
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: New Hoong Fatt Holdings Bhd's unit Jhi Soon Manufacturing Industries Sdn Bhd plans to invest up to RM20 million in a venture capital fund established. It will be set up through a special purpose venture capital fund vehicle Cypress Drive Ventures Sdn Bhd (FundCo). The investment committee will comprise two members nominated by New Hoong Fatt and two nominated by the fund promoter Cypress Asia Capital Sdn Bhd.

items.title: Health Ministry van, bus collide on Senai-Desaru Expressway
items.summary: KULAI: A Health Ministry van carrying one passenger and a bus were involved in a collision at KM23.3 of the Senai-Desaru Expressway (southbound) near here today. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Tan Seng Lee, who confirmed the incident, said no one was injured in the 12.30pm accident. "The bus was not carrying any passengers, while the Health Ministry van had one passenger on board.

items.title: Azeez released from police custody, lawyer says
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim has been released from police custody, his lawyer said. Azeez is a member of Umno's supreme council. Amer said Azeez had expressed relief upon his release after two days at the Dang Wangi police station.

items.title: Farmer shot dead outside family member’s rented house in Banting
items.summary: Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar said the victim died at the scene after being hit by several shots in the incident between 10.30 pm and 11 pm. “Police received information about the incident at about 11.15 pm. Following the incident, police detained a local man in his 20s to 30s around the Banting area late last night.

items.title: No indication of volcanic ash entering Malaysian airspace, says MetMalaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — There are no indications that toxic volcanic ash from an eruption in Indonesia is moving across Malaysian airspace, as recently claimed on social media. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said current monitoring showed that volcanic ash, including from Gunung Anak Krakatau, was moving towards the Indian Ocean northwest of Sumatra, rather than towards Malaysia. “Monitoring shows that the ash is moving towards open waters, not towards the peninsula, Sabah or Sarawak.

items.title: Rosmah’s solar graft case: High Court to hear fresh evidence from key witness on Sept 17
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The High Court today set September 17 to hear additional evidence from the star prosecution witness, Rayyan Radzwill Abdullah, in Datin Seri Rosmah Mansor’s solar hybrid project graft trial. Judge Datuk Aslam Zainuddin fixed the date after Rosmah’s counsel, Datuk Jagjit Singh, told the court that the Court of Appeal had allowed Rosmah’s application to adduce additional evidence in her appeal and directed that the additional evidence be recorded by the High Court. If not, we will proceed as ordered by the Court of Appeal.

items.title: PAS at Umno assembly: Friendly visit or ‘preview’ of next election?
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — When PAS delegates began arriving at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur last night for Umno’s annual assembly this week, the gesture drew more than polite greetings from party members. For some Umno delegates, the presence of PAS delegates was a sign that the idea of Malay-Muslim unity was gaining ground again. For others, it was a matter of returning a courtesy after Umno representatives attended PAS’s muktamar last week.

items.title: Four Chinese nationals face kidnapping charge after Singaporean allegedly held for RM3.28m ransom
items.summary: BALIK PULAU, Sept 10 — Four Chinese nationals were charged at the Sessions Court here today with kidnapping a Singaporean man in July and demanding a ransom of SGD1 million (about RM3.28 million). The accused, Liu Ting Jun, 46; Huang Jian, 39; Wang Hao Yu, 32; and Guan Siqi, 24, the only woman among them, however, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read to them in Mandarin before Judge Ahzal Fariz Ahmad Khairuddin. According to the charge sheet, the accused, as well as two others still at large and another two individuals who have since died, are accused of jointly abducting and wrongfully confining Quek Aik Teng at the Penang International Airport in Bayan Lepas at 4.15 pm on July 26.

items.title: Drug syndicates use public as mules to smuggle cannabis to Europe, says Bukit Aman
items.summary: BACHOK, Sept 10 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) have found that drug trafficking syndicates operating by air to Europe frequently use members of the public as drug mules, particularly to transport cannabis flowers, which are in high demand on the continent. Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department Director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said, however, that not all pilots arrested for involvement in drug smuggling were transporting drugs to Europe. He said most air-based drug trafficking cases involving Europe centred on cannabis flowers due to the high demand for the illicit substance in the market.

items.title: Layang-Layang Aerospace voluntarily grounds BO-105 fleet after Sarawak helicopter crash
items.summary: Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) chief executive officer Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud said the decision was taken by the operator voluntarily and should not be interpreted as an indication of technical failure. Norazman said CAAM records showed that the helicopter’s Certificate of Airworthiness was valid until Aug 4, 2027, while its Certificate of Registration remained valid until July 28, 2029. Norazman said CAAM was monitoring the operator’s grounding and inspection programme, while also verifying the relevant regulatory, operator and pilot records.

items.title: Court rejects police bid to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand, former TH chairman set for release
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Former Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim is expected to be released this evening after his remand period was not extended, said his lawyer Datuk Amer Hamzah Arshad. He said the police’s application to extend Abdul Azeez’s remand period for another three days to assist in the investigation under Section 420 of the Penal Code had been rejected, and the former Baling Member of Parliament is expected to be released before 5pm this evening once the previous remand period expires. Abdul Azeez and two former TH officers were previously remanded for two days to assist in the investigation into a fraud case related to TH hibah.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected across KL, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya and seven states until 6pm today. It said in a statement that the adverse weather is forecast to affect Kuala Muda, Baling, Sik, Yan and Langkawi in Kedah; Timur Laut, Barat Daya, Seberang Perai Utara and Seberang Perai Tengah in Penang; and Kuala Pilah, Seremban, Jempol and Jelebu in Negeri Sembilan. Similar weather conditions are also forecast in Larut Matang, Selama, Bagan Datuk, Manjung, Perak Tengah, Hilir Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Hulu Perak, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim in Perak; Sepang, Petaling, Hulu Langat, Gombak, Klang and Kuala Langat in Selangor, as well as Cameron Highlands, Raub, Bentong, Bera, Jerantut and Lipis in Pahang.

items.title: Sarawak Flying Doctor Service operations suspended after fatal helicopter crash, says health minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — All Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in Sarawak have been temporarily suspended following a helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Miri, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said today. “Emergency medical evacuation services for urgent cases will continue through cooperation between the Health Ministry and the Fire and Rescue Department,” he said. Dzulkefly said the ministry would also discuss the possible use of Armed Forces assets to transport patients requiring emergency treatment to suitable healthcare facilities.

items.title: Digital Ministry seeks Budget 2027 incentives to cut cost of digital tools for small traders
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 10 — The Digital Ministry has proposed incentives under Budget 2027 to make digital tools more affordable and encourage their adoption among small traders, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said today. He said the proposals were presented during a meeting with Finance Ministry officials two weeks ago as part of the government’s Budget engagement process. “Let the Finance Ministry make its decision and the prime minister announce it during or before the Budget,” he said.

items.title: Hannah Yeoh confirms Pardons Board meeting as speculation over Najib’s bid mounts
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh has confirmed that the Federal Territories Pardons Board (FTPB) will convene tomorrow morning. “Yes, I can confirm that tomorrow at 8.30am, there will be a pardons board meeting. FMT previously reported that former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s application is expected to be among the primary matters tabled before the board during this week's sitting.

items.title: Puteri Umno wishes Najib well ahead of expected clemency bid discussion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno’s women’s youth wing, Puteri Umno, today extended its best wishes for former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid ahead of a meeting expected to discuss his application. This follows a report by Free Malaysia Today that the Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s clemency application during its meeting this week. Puteri Umno chief Datuk Nurul Amal Mohd Fauzi expressed the wing’s positive wishes during a press conference at the Umno General Assembly at the World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur (WTCKL) today.

items.title: Zahid to meet Negeri Sembilan MB over statement on proclamation involving Tuanku Muhriz
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said today he will meet Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim during the party’s general assembly to seek an explanation over his statement regarding a proclamation involving the state’s ruler. Zahid said Ismail would meet him during the assembly, which began yesterday, although he did not specify when the meeting would take place. Asked when the meeting would take place, Zahid said: “The general assembly has already begun.

items.title: Umno president Zahid says being optimistic about Najib’s pardon chances tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi today said he was hoping for the best when the Pardons Board considers former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s clemency bid tomorrow. The Federal Territories Pardons Board is expected to discuss Najib’s latest application for tomorrow. Najib, 72, was convicted of misappropriating RM42 million belonging to SRC International and sentenced to 12 years in prison, along with a RM210 million fine.

items.title: King presents appointment instruments to Court of Appeal, High Court judges
items.summary: The ceremony began with the presentation to Court of Appeal judge Alice Loke Yee Ching, followed by High Court judge Elaine Yap Chin Gaik. She was appointed a judicial commissioner of the Shah Alam High Court on July 10, 2020. She was elevated to Shah Alam High Court judge on Jan 17, 2023, before being appointed to the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s Special Powers Division on Aug 18, 2025.

items.title: Perak Assembly approves PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul as senator with 33 votes
items.summary: IPOH, September 10 — The Perak Legislative Assembly today approved the appointment of Perak PKR chairman Mohamad Hairul Amir Sabri as a senator after he secured 33 votes in a secret ballot. The 38-year-old defeated Perak PAS Dewan Ulama chairman Muhammad Zulkifli Muhammad Zakaria, the Opposition coalition’s candidate, who received 26 votes. Mohamad Hairul has also served as Perak PKR chairman since 2024.

items.title: Transboundary haze discussed on sidelines of Asean health ministers meeting, says Dzulkefly
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The transboundary haze issue is not on the formal agenda of the 17th ASEAN Health Ministers Meeting (AHMM) and Related Meetings, but it is being discussed on the sidelines among health ministers of member states. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the matter could subsequently be taken up at the senior officers’ meeting. However, Dzulkefly said the issue could be addressed within the scope of the existing health clusters.

items.title: Dr Akmal: Umno Youth ready to work with PAS in Melaka, state is next test for Malay-Muslim unity
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — Umno Youth is ready to work with PAS in the coming Melaka state election and believes its support among young voters can help deliver another electoral victory, Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Saleh said today. So I ask Datuk Seri (Zahid), Melaka should be blue as well,” he said during his speech at the Umno Youth general assembly.He said Umno Youth was prepared to repeat the strong performance it recorded among young voters in the Johor and Negri Sembilan state elections. Dr Akmal said the wing was prepared to cooperate with PAS in Melaka, while making clear that he was not seeking candidacy for himself.

items.title: Malaysia’s unsold completed homes rise 8.6pc in H1 2026, but market is resilient, says finance minister II
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — More completed homes and serviced apartments were left unsold in the first half of 2026 compared with the preceding six months, according to the Property Market Report for the First Half of 2026. The report, released by the Valuation and Property Services Department (JPPH) today, showed that the number of unsold completed homes rose by 8.6 per cent, from 30,471 units in the second half of 2025 to 33,094 units in the first half of 2026. Residential properties accounted for 59.3 per cent of all transactions, with 110,998 deals recorded, and contributed 44.8 per cent of the total transaction value, or RM47.11 billion.

items.title: Kangar Bersatu deputy chief, 90 branch chiefs leave party over loss of trust in leadership
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 10 — Kangar Bersatu division deputy chief Faisol Rahman, together with the division committee and 90 of its 99 branch chiefs, announced tonight that they are leaving the party with immediate effect. Also announcing their departure were the division’s Armada, Srikandi and Srikandi Muda leadership lines, including Armada Kangar deputy chief Mohd Firdaus Ismail and all Armada committee members. “Having spent so long building the party at the grassroots level, we feel that trust in the party’s leadership has been lost,” he said.

items.title: MOH still awaiting official post-mortem report on five Long Lellang crash victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is still awaiting the official report on the post-mortem findings of the five victims who were killed in the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter crash in Long Lellang, Ulu Baram, Sarawak. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was still awaiting official confirmation on the matter before providing further details to the public. Also present were MOH secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad and Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abdul Wahab.
